summary: Cold read of the recorded assistant-streaming-and-shell contract returned NOT CONVERGED with six repository findings and four handover questions. All six were verified and held, and one is a LIVE DEFECT in merged code: use-ask.ts:31 sends every successful prior turn while task 1's schema rejects more than eight, so the ninth question in a conversation 400s today. The read also found that a universal switch to streaming would move the stored-selection re-run off the buffered route, that an abort renders as an error, that terminal SSE frames lack renderer fields, that UTF-8 chunk splitting was unaddressed, and that dock geometry cannot be unit-proven in jsdom. Criteria rose from seven to eight and required leaves from six to nine.

criteria_map.Both Ask surfaces consume POST /api/chat: Streaming and SSE framing, widened after the read: byte-level chunk handling so a multi-byte UTF-8 character split across two chunks cannot corrupt a frame, no phase after the terminal frame, and the delayed-phase timer cleared on EVERY terminal path.
criteria_map.An answer that resolves within 250ms ren: The no-flicker rule, unchanged in substance: it stays a CLIENT render delay because chat.service.ts:103 emits routing before the deterministic classifiers, so greetings and refusals do receive a phase today.
criteria_map.The streaming client preserves EVERYTHIN: Transport parity, plus the branch the read found missing: use-ask.ts:27 has ONE run() behind both ask() and rerun(), so a universal switch to streaming would have moved the stored-selection re-run off the buffered route it must stay on. Ordinary HTTP errors render as the buffered client renders them.
criteria_map.Leaving the assistant cancels the in-fli: Cancellation, now with a named boundary and two corrections. The assistant area is exactly /ask and /mis-reports because AskProvider lives in the persistent shell and an unmounting panel cannot own the boundary. An abort currently falls into the generic catch and renders as an error, and terminal SSE error frames do not carry the fields the seven-class renderer needs - both must be normalised.
criteria_map.The shell's freshness pill shows the rea: The freshness pill, which has SIX states to render rather than five: the route's available, no-active-batches, unsupported, unconfigured and lookup-failed, plus a client-side 'could not check' that must never be shown as the server's lookup-failed. Explicit timezone, no silent retry, no unqualified cached value. A partially loaded warehouse is D-0042 and out of scope.
criteria_map.The docked Ask panel fills its column on: The dock, unchanged in intent: max-height with align-self flex-start is a ceiling, not a height, which is the gap the human reported. Mobile stacking is untouched.
criteria_map.The client TRIMS prior turns to the shar: NEW criterion for a LIVE DEFECT the read surfaced: use-ask.ts:31 sends every successful turn while task 1's schema rejects more than eight, so the ninth question in a conversation 400s against merged code today. The client now trims newest-first to the constants exported from @3f/contract, keeping oldest-first order because the server reads at(-1) as the latest turn.
criteria_map.The surfaces are proven by vitest leaves: The proof, grown from six leaves to nine, and with one criterion moved OUT of unit testing: jsdom does not compute flex layout, so a vitest leaf for dock geometry could only assert CSS source text and would be a false green. The live functional check is the geometry proof at desktop and mobile. The check REPORTS observed latency rather than enforcing a sub-5s bound, since measurement after task 1 gave 1.0-5.4s.

current_flow: Tasks 1 and 2 shipped: the selector is capped at 512 with a scoped retry and bounded cancellation, and GET /api/warehouse/freshness serves load freshness in five states. Neither is visible. The Ask surfaces still POST to buffered /api/chat and show one static pending state, nothing references /api/chat/stream, the shell still renders a hard-coded aria-disabled chip, and the docked panel still uses a max-height ceiling that leaves a gap.
new_abstractions: An SSE client for this codebase - the first streaming transport, with byte-level chunk buffering and terminal-failure normalisation on a provider shared by two surfaces.
A route-set cancellation boundary: the first place navigation itself decides whether work continues.
A six-state status chip where a client failure is deliberately distinct from the server's own failure state.
gaps: use-ask.ts:31 sends EVERY successful prior turn while task 1 shipped chat.schemas.ts rejecting more than ASK_PRIOR_TURNS_MAX_ENTRIES, so the ninth successful question in a conversation 400s against merged code today; the client must trim to the shared limits and prove it.

A universal switch to streaming breaks saved and pinned reruns: use-ask.ts:27 has one run() behind both ask() and rerun(), but a stored-selection re-run bypasses the model and must stay on buffered /api/chat.

An abort currently falls into the generic catch and renders as an error; terminal SSE error frames also lack the fields the seven-class AskResponse renderer requires, and delayed-phase timers are not cleared on every terminal path.
Chunk handling was specified at the frame level only, so a multi-byte UTF-8 character split across two chunks could corrupt a frame.
The promised coverage omitted buffered reruns, ordinary HTTP errors, post-terminal phase suppression and UTF-8 chunk splitting.
Dock geometry cannot be proven by a vitest leaf: frontend/vitest.config.ts uses jsdom, which does not compute flex layout, so such a test could only assert CSS source text.
contradictions: The confirmed spec required populating provenance.dataAsOf while this task's contract correctly defers it under D-0041, and mandated maxTokens 2048 and a sub-5s live check while the shipped predecessor uses 512 - the spec was amended and re-confirmed to resolve both.
resolutions: REPO-ANSWERED - a new criterion requires the client to trim prior turns newest-first to the constants exported from @3f/contract, with a leaf driving nine qualifying turns and asserting the request body, fixing a live 400.

REPO-ANSWERED - the streaming switch is explicitly NOT universal: the stored-selection re-run stays on buffered /api/chat, proven by its own leaf, and ordinary HTTP errors render as the buffered client renders them.

REPO-ANSWERED - expected aborts are recognised and swallowed rather than rendered; terminal SSE error frames are normalised into the renderer's required fields; delayed-phase timers are cleared on every terminal path.
REPO-ANSWERED - chunk handling is specified at the BYTE level so a split multi-byte character cannot corrupt a frame, with a leaf covering it alongside post-terminal phase suppression.

HUMAN (kl-rahulanand) - the assistant area is exactly /ask and /mis-reports: navigation within the set never cancels, any other authenticated route aborts. The routes are named because AskProvider lives in the persistent shell.

HUMAN (kl-rahulanand) - the pill renders each of the five server states distinctly plus a separate client 'could not check', with an explicit timezone, the inherited single 401 refresh, and no silent retry or unqualified cached value.
HUMAN (kl-rahulanand) - dock geometry is proven by the LIVE functional check at desktop and mobile breakpoints, not by a vitest leaf that would assert CSS source text and be a false green.

HUMAN (kl-rahulanand) - 512 is the governed cap, the spec was amended and re-confirmed to match shipped code, and the live check REPORTS observed latency (1.0-5.4s measured) rather than enforcing a hard bound this model's variance cannot support.

rounds.question: Closing the `assistant-streaming-and-shell` grill — the last task. Six repo findings folded in, and one is a **live defect in merged code**: `use-ask.ts:31` sends every successful turn while task 1's schema rejects more than 8, so **the ninth question in a conversation 400s right now**. This task's client trim fixes it. Also caught: streaming everything would have moved the stored-selection re-run off the buffered route it must stay on (one `run()` serves both `ask()` and `rerun()`); an abort currently renders as an **error** via the generic catch; terminal SSE error frames don't carry the fields the seven-class renderer needs; and a multi-byte UTF-8 character split across chunks would corrupt a frame. Your four decisions are in — including that **dock geometry is proven by the live check**, since jsdom can't compute flex layout and a vitest leaf would just assert CSS text. Criteria 7→8, leaves 6→9.
